title: Lower Falinge’s proposed 270 homes would replace 150: what residents gain and lose
body:
RBH’s next Lower Falinge phase is reported to envisage 270 affordable-rented homes across two parcels, replacing 150 homes proposed for demolition. If implemented on that basis, the eventual net addition is around 120 homes, not 270.

The screening-stage proposal includes houses and apartments. It does not itself grant planning permission for the development. The current reference identified in reporting is OTH/2026/0781; final layouts and consent remain separate steps.

There is a directly relevant legal history. Claimants’ barristers reported that the council conceded a challenge to its earlier demolition prior approval over its EIA reasoning. The later October 2025 decision was reported as a refusal. This concerned the decision-making process and should not be recast as a finding of criminal misconduct by a builder.

RBH says regeneration is intended to create safe, warm family homes and has held resident consultation. Existing residents need clear rehousing commitments, costs and any opportunity to return. A temporary loss of homes before replacement is also important for borough-wide supply.

The regulator’s January 2026 judgement confirmed RBH’s G2 governance and V2 viability grades, recognising improvement while identifying risks. It did not assess consumer standards through that stability check.

The infrastructure test must consider the whole regeneration programme and its phases, including services during demolition and reconstruction, rather than treating every parcel as unrelated.

Location: Lower Falinge, north of Rochdale town centre

Planning stage: Regeneration proposals and EIA screening request; full scheme approval not established

Homes: 270 proposed replacement homes; 150 proposed demolitions; about 120 eventual net gain

Let or for sale: Affordable rent proposed; not automatically social rent

Land: Existing housing estate and previously developed urban parcels

Final planning agreement: The new 270-home proposal is at screening/proposal stage in the reviewed records; a final permission and executed agreement were not established. Earlier demolition litigation does not grant approval to this scheme.

Exact rents / prices: Exact new rents, service charges, temporary rehousing costs and return-tenancy terms are not provided in the reviewed council/government records or established from the public proposal.

Affordable breakdown: 270 affordable-rented replacements proposed, not necessarily Social Rent. Demolishing 150 gives about 120 eventual net additions. Bedroom/tenure distribution and binding return rights remain unverified.

Funded school capacity: No scheme-specific funded additional school places, named capital project and opening date were established from the accessible official records reviewed.

Funded healthcare capacity: No site-specific funded NHS expansion, additional staffed appointment capacity or delivery date was established from the accessible council/government records reviewed. Proximity to a surgery is not a capacity assessment.

Funded transport capacity: No funded new transport-service capacity or complete construction-phase access plan established. Services for existing residents also matter during rehousing and demolition.

The outstanding details identified above are not yet available to Rochdale Daily. This article will be updated when the information becomes available.

Research checked 14 October 2026. Advertised prices are snapshots, not achieved sale prices.

Read the borough-wide housing investigation and the other developments: https://rochdaledaily.co.uk/articles/rochdale-housing-developments-affordability-schools-gp-transport.html
